outcomes: An experimenter can explicitly add the Python extension and run Python lint, test, serve, run, dependency-install, package and publish jobs through Putnami
Python dependency installation and upgrades remain scoped to explicitly configured Python workspace projects
Python integration remains usable for experiments without claiming stable compatibility, default adoption, or parity with Go or TypeScript
nonGoals: Providing a Python application framework or framework-package compatibility layer
Making Python a default workspace path
Providing feature, API, or operational parity with Go or TypeScript
Changing CLI extension discovery, workspace initialization, or upgrade orchestration

requirements.text: Documentation and generated project manifests require an explicit Python extension selection; no Python template or sample is presented as the default project path.

Python workspace installation and upgrade jobs operate on the Python projects selected from the workspace and report a skipped or failed result instead of inventing a missing project. A project whose [project] name is no valid project name, such as a template's placeholder, is no uv workspace member.
The extension delegates Python dependency, lint, test, and workload execution to uv, Ruff, pytest, and the configured application entrypoint, exposing their result through Putnami jobs.

text: Every task that runs uv requires the uv runtime toolchain bound to the uv pin of the workspace lock, so it runs and is keyed on that release.
The toolchain lists uv on PATH, then the uv the CLI provisions under the Putnami home; a uv of another release never runs.
The extension installs no uv: workspace-install runs the resolved uv and, outside a hosted run, declares its release as the [tool.uv] required-version of the root pyproject.toml.
With none, a job fails naming the release and `putnami install`.

requirements.text: When the repository pins uv for its own tools in .prototools, mise.toml, .mise.toml, .tool-versions or a moon toolchain file, workspace-install declares no [tool.uv] required-version, which would make uv refuse the repository's own setup.

A [tool.uv] required-version in the root pyproject.toml that names no single uv release, such as a range, or a release older than 0.11.8, the oldest one Putnami runs, fails workspace-install and every task that runs uv with a diagnostic that names the exact declaration to write, and runs no uv.

text: The extension answers `__putnami toolchain-resolve` with one uv pin: the release the root pyproject.toml declares as [tool.uv] required-version, else the default.
A committed lock version 5 pin of that release is kept as committed.
The default is pinned offline from the digests the extension ships, another declared release from its release checksum file;
offline that is a problem whose remedy is `putnami install` with network access.
A declaration or host platform it cannot pin is a problem with a remedy.

package with the docker channel assembles an OCI image of an application with no Docker daemon, on the official python:<pinned>-slim image of the Python minor uv selects, pinned by digest, or on a digest-pinned base the project names;
a base with no digest fails.
The image runs python on the entrypoint option of package, src/main.py by default, as an unprivileged user.

An image holds the production dependencies of uv.lock, installed as wheels for its platform and the Python release of its base, checked against their locked hashes, and the local packages uv export lists built from a staging copy.
A path dependency outside the project's dependency closure fails.
An image holds the application files, without tests, environment files or registry credentials.
The cache key of package-docker covers the files the image ships, the uv workspace files and the path dependencies.

publish with the docker channel pushes the packaged image to the declared OCI registry through the shared publisher, and the workspace probe declares it as an oci release-set member of an application that publishes the docker channel.

requirements.text: The extension's support status is experimental, non-default, and unsupported for parity; upgrade documentation must not imply a supported Python framework release set.
